'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****A [[Taliban]] militant is stabbed by protestors in [[Asadabad, Afghanistan|Asadabad]] while celebrating [[Afghan Independence Day|Independence Day]]. Fellow Taliban militants open fire on the crowd after the stabbing, killing two people and wounding eight others. Additionally, two people are injured during a protest in [[Jalalabad]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/19/us-troops-to-stay-in-afghanistan-till-all-americans-out-live (Al Jazeera)]
****More incidents are reported at the airport in [[Kabul]], as civilians try to escape the country. A total of 12 people have been confirmed to have been killed at the airport since [[Fall of Kabul (2021)|the fall of the city]], primarily due to [[stampede]]s and gun incidents. [https://www.businessinsider.com/kabul-airport-12-dead-since-sunday-taliban-tells-people-leave-2021-8?r=US&IR=T (''Business Insider'')]
****[[Ahmad Massoud]], the 32-year-old son of anti-[[Soviet]] [[mujahideen]] leader [[Ahmad Shah Massoud]], vows to resist a potential assault of the Taliban on [[Panjshir Province|Panjshir]]. Massoud, who is allied with self-proclaimed acting [[President of Afghanistan|president]] [[Amrullah Saleh]], says that the Taliban will face a "staunch resistance" if they attack. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/son-slain-afghan-hero-massoud-vows-resistance-seeks-support-2021-08-19/ (Reuters)]
****[[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Joe Biden]] says that the Taliban "must decide if it wants international recognition", but that the group had not changed its priorities during the past 20 years. [https://www.rte.ie/news/world/2021/0819/1241621-afghanistan/ (RTE)]
***[[Operation Allies Refuge]]
****[[The Pentagon]] announces that 7,000 civilians have been evacuated since August 14. [https://www.axios.com/kabul-airport-evacuation-numbers-afghanistan-76942db3-9db4-4915-a3be-c5f86cb425a6.html (Axios)]
**The Taliban declares the formation of the [[Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan]]. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/siladityaray/2021/08/19/taliban-declares-formation-of-islamic-emirate-groups-fighters-open-fire-at-protest-rally/?sh=699daff77001 (''Forbes'')]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Three people are killed and 50 more wounded during a [[grenade]] attack at a [[Shia Islam in Pakistan|Shiite]] religious procession in [[Bahawalnagar]], [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/19/blast-hits-ashura-procession-in-pakistan-dozens-wounded (Al Jazeera)]
*[[War in Somalia (2009–present)|War in Somalia]]
**A [[suicide bombing|suicide bomber]] blows himself up at a restaurant in [[Mogadishu]], [[Somalia]], killing three people and wounding several more. The restaurant was frequented by members of the security forces as it is near to a security agency. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/africa/2021-08/20/c_1310137369.htm (Xinhua)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Jihadism|Jihadists]] [[ambush]] a convoy in [[Mopti]], killing 11 soldiers and wounding 10 others. A [[roadside bomb]] hit the convoy, and gunmen then opened fire. [https://m.republicworld.com/world-news/africa/mali-armed-forces-convoy-ambushed-in-mopti-11-soldiers-killed-9-others-critical.html (Republic World)]
*Thirty-two people are killed in [[Far North Region, Cameroon|Far North]], [[Cameroon]], in clashes between fishermen and herders since the beginning of the month. Nineteen villages have been burned. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/cameroon-ethnic-clashes-kill-least-32-villages-are-torched-unhcr-2021-08-19/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[2020–2021 global chip shortage]]
**[[Toyota]] reduces its production quota for next month by 40% due to the resurgence of COVID-19 in Asia severely impacting the company's supply chains, especially those involved in [[Integrated circuit|chip]] production. Up to this point, the company was one of the only major car manufacturers to avoid scaling back production during the pandemic. [[Volkswagen]] warns that it might also have to reduce its production quotas for similar reasons. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-58266794 (BBC News)]
*Content subscription service [[OnlyFans]] announces that it will ban [[pornography|sexually explicit material]] beginning in October. The policy changes, according to UK-based company, are "to comply with the requests of the banking partners and payout providers". [https://variety.com/2021/digital/news/onlyfans-ban-pornography-sexually-explicit-1235044904/ (Variety)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Haiti earthquake]]
**The death toll of the [[earthquake]] in [[Haiti]] reaches 2,189. [https://apnews.com/article/caribbean-haiti-7dd9920a35433df7d1f18ad2599d94f1 (Associated Press)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
*****The number of people over the age of 16 who have received their first dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] in [[Australia]] surpasses 50%, with a record 309,010 doses administered yesterday. [https://amp.abc.net.au/article/100391262 (ABC News Australia)]
****Australia reports a new single-day record of 754 new cases of [[COVID-19]], including a record for the second consecutive day of 681 new cases of COVID-19 in [[New South Wales]], surpassing the previous record set in August 2020 during the second wave of the pandemic in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]]. [https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/7392876/australia-in-record-day-for-cases-and-jabs/?src=rss (''The Canberra Times'')] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] surpasses 400 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/449476/covid-19-fiji-reports-8-deaths-and-653-new-cases (RNZ)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in New Zealand]]
****[[Prime Minister of New Zealand|Prime Minister]] [[Jacinda Arden]]'s [[Cabinet of New Zealand|Cabinet]] grants approval for children between the ages of 12 and 15 to receive the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine]] beginning on September 1. [https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/new-zealand/2021/08/coronavirus-12-to-15-year-olds-now-eligible-for-pfizer-vaccine-in-new-zealand.html (Newshub)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] receives their first shipment of 1.56 million doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine]]. [https://kabar24.bisnis.com/read/20210819/15/1431774/perdana-156-juta-vaksin-pfizer-akhirnya-tiba-di-indonesia (Kabar24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] surpasses 100,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/irans-covid-19-death-toll-rises-above-100000-health-ministry-2021-08-19/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 25,156 new cases of COVID-19. [https://jen.jiji.com/jc/eng?g=eco&k=2021081901129 (Jiji Press)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 22,242 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,489,460. [https://www.theedgemarkets.com/article/malaysias-daily-new-covid19-cases-climb-further-22948-aug-19-%E2%80%94-highest-level-onset-pandemic- (The Edge Markets)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[COVID-19 community quarantines in the Philippines]]
****[[Metro Manila]] and the provinces of [[Bataan]] and [[Laguna (province)|Laguna]] will have their restrictions eased under the slightly restrictive Modified Enhanced Community Quarantine beginning on August 21 for Metro Manila and Laguna and August 23 for Bataan. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/metro-manila-laguna-bataan-modified-enhanced-community-quarantine-mecq-august-31-2021 (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] begins reopening its borders with the launch of Vaccinated Travel Lanes for [[COVID-19 vaccine|fully vaccinated]] travellers from [[Germany]] and [[Brunei]], while quarantine-free restrictions will be eased for travellers from [[Hong Kong]], [[Macau]], [[Mainland China]] outside of [[Jiangsu]] Province, [[New Zealand]] and [[Taiwan]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/germany-brunei-travel-lane-fully-vaccinated-shn-hong-kong-macao-2122796 (CNA)]
****Beginning tomorrow, all travellers entering [[Singapore]] who are fully vaccinated with a [[World Health Organization]]-recognized [[COVID-19 vaccine]] will be issued a tamper-proof vaccination sticker in their passport upon the presentation of a [[COVID-19 vaccine card|COVID-19 vaccination certificate]]. [https://www.todayonline.com/singapore/covid-19-ica-issue-tamper-proof-vaccination-sticker-newly-arrived-travellers-immunised (''TODAY'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports a record 10,654 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 312,611. [http://vietnamnews.vn/society/1016196/viet-nam-reports-record-high-number-of-covid-19-cases.html (Viet Nam News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***[[France]] designates [[Algeria]] and [[Morocco]] as "high-risk" countries, which means that beginning from August 21, unvaccinated travellers will have to prove that their trip is essential, requiring a proof of negative [[COVID-19 test]], and must accept a 10-day self-[[quarantine]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20210819-france-adds-algeria-morocco-to-list-of-high-risk-covid-countries (Radio France Internationale)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Kenya]]
***[[Kenya]]'s [[Pharmacy and Poisons Board]] grants emergency use authorization for the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna]] and [[Sinopharm]] [[BBIBP-CorV]] vaccines. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-08-19/kenya-approves-moderna-sinopharm-vaccines-amid-fourth-wave (Bloomberg)]
*[[Ivory Coast]] reports an outbreak of the highly pathogenic [[Influenza A virus subtype H5N1|H5N1]] after a large number of [[poultry]] birds started dying in the [[Grand-Bassam]] commune near the capital [[Abidjan]] on July 20. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ivory-coast-confirms-h5n1-avian-flu-outbreak-2021-08-19/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Hong Kong]] and [[Singapore]] abandon plans to resume a "travel bubble" for [[quarantine]]-free travel between the two cities due to differing COVID-19 policies. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/transport/singapore-hong-kong-will-no-longer-launch-travel-bubble-due-to-different-covid (''The Straits Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*The [[United States Supreme Court Building|U.S. Supreme Court Building]], the headquarters of the [[Republican National Committee]], and other locations in [[Washington, D.C.]]'s [[Capitol Hill]] area are evacuated after a man parked his truck in front of the [[Library of Congress]] and threatened to detonate a bomb while making anti-government statements. The man surrendered to the police several hours after he began his standoff. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/08/19/us-capitol-police-respond-to-report-of-suspicious-vehicle-near-library-of-congress.html (CNBC)]

'''Science and technology'''
*Rain falls on the summit of [[Greenland]] for the first time in recorded history. The rain shower dumped more than 7 billion tonnes of water on the ice sheet. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/08/19/weather/greenland-summit-rain-climate-change/index.html (CNN)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2020 Summer Paralympics]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**The [[Tokyo Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games]] reports the first Paralympic-linked case of COVID-19 at the [[Harumi Futo|Olympic village]] that is not a Paralympic athlete or a Japanese resident. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58265320 (BBC News)]
